html:
"Saharan Nomadic Tribes" is the map's label for the desert peoples of the Sahara around 700 CE. Most were Berbers who lived by herding camels, goats and sheep between wells and oases, and by guiding, taxing or raiding the caravans that crossed the desert.

The camel had spread through North Africa in the first centuries CE, and with it the Berber tribes became masters of the deep desert. The Sanhaja held the western Sahara, and the ancestors of the Tuareg the central part.

Around 700 the Arab conquests reached the Maghreb, and the desert tribes slowly took up Islam. Over the next centuries the trans-Saharan trade in gold, salt and slaves linked North Africa with Ghana and the other states of West Africa, and these nomads were its guides and middlemen. They follow the older Saharan pastoral nomads of the map.
